application.name: ofetch
application.summary: A TypeScript HTTP-fetch utility that wraps Fetch with parsed response data, configurable request options, hooks, retries, and normalized errors.
application.purpose: Make HTTP requests convenient and type-safe across supported runtimes, while providing shared handling for request setup, response parsing, and failures.

domains.name: HTTP requests
domains.description: Building and sending requests with merged options, headers, base URLs, query parameters, and request hooks.

domains.name: Response handling
domains.description: Parsing response bodies into the requested or inferred type and exposing parsed data or the raw response.

domains.name: Errors and retries
domains.description: Retrying eligible failures and producing errors with request, response, status, and parsed response data.

domains.name: Runtime adapters
domains.description: Providing fetch implementations and related primitives for global and Node.js environments.

domains.name: Developer experience
domains.description: Supporting typed request results, configurable hooks, and reusable fetch instances with defaults.

applicationFacts: The default $fetch/ofetch API resolves to parsed response data; its raw method returns the response object.
The fetch client supports typed response results and response types including JSON, text, blob, array buffer, and stream.
Request options include base URLs, query parameters, merged headers, timeouts, retries, and lifecycle hooks.
JSON-serializable bodies for payload methods are automatically serialized, with JSON headers added when absent.
Response parsing can be selected explicitly or inferred from the Content-Type header.
Errors for unsuccessful HTTP responses can include the request, response, status information, and parsed response data.
The Node.js entry point uses global fetch when available and otherwise provides a node-fetch-native fallback.
